 Creamline seeks twice-to-beat advantage in semis
 By Nicole Anne D.G. Bugauisan
 November 21, 2026
 940
 Resize 
 Small 
 Medium 
 Large 
 Read this in The Manila Times digital edition. 
 CREAMLINE’s Bernadeth Pons knows that Farm Fresh’s Trisha Tubu can be a beast inside the playing court and the Cool Smashers have mapped up a plan to contain her when they clash in the 2026-27 Premier Volleyball League (PVL) All-Filipino Conference-Siklab Series on Saturday at the PhilSports Arena in Pasig City.
 Game time is 1 p.m.
 Defending champion Creamline (4-3) already secured a spot in the semifinal round along with Nxled (7-0), Choco Mucho (5-3) and Farm Fresh (5-2) but is aiming for a big win on Saturday to earn a twice-to-beat incentive in the final four.
 A win by the Cool Smashers will forge a three-way tie for second place with Choco Mucho and Farm Fresh. In this scenario, Creamline will get the No. 2 spot and the twice-to-beat edge while Farm Fresh is relegated to No. 4 and Choco Mucho to No. 3.
 In the point tally, Choco Mucho finished the elims with 15 points, while Farm Fresh and Creamline currently has 14 and 13 points, respectively.

 If Creamline wins in three or four sets, it will get two more points but a win by five sets earns only one point. Creamline, however, has the advantage over Choco Mucho in the set-point ratio which assures the Cool Smashers the No. 2 spot and the twice-to-beat edge.
 If Creamline loses on Saturday, Nxled will still be No.1 followed by Farm Fresh at No.2 and Choco Mucho at No. 3.
 Advertisement 
 Pons understands the importance of Saturday’s game against Farm Fresh and the Cool Smashers are ready to take on Tubu and the Foxies.
 In seven games, Tubu averaged 18 points per game for Farm Fresh, highlighted by a 30-point outing in a win against the Savi Davison-led PLDT last Nov. 10.
 “Trisha is very athletic, she jumps so high, and she’s a lefty too. In her past few games, they’ve been feeding her a lot of balls because her percentage is really high and her efficiency is excellent. But volleyball is a team sport,” said Pons, who boasts of having one Conference Most Valuable Player and two Finals MVP honors with Creamline.
 While the Sherwin Meneses-mentored squad suffered three straight setbacks after a remarkable 4-0 start in the tournament, Pons is confident the Cool Smashers can end the skid and defeat the Foxies.
 Advertisement 
 Backing Pons are a formidable cast of players lead by Alyssa Valdez, Tots Carlos, Jema Galanza, Michele Gumabao and playmakers Jia de Guzman and Kyle Negrito.
 “We really need to be complete as a unit. By Saturday, all of us have to be threats to the opponent. What’s important is how we play, regardless of what the other team does,” said Pons.
 “That’s also what they want to see more of, and that’s what Coach always reminds us, that every one of us should be a threat to the opposing team.” Tubu, on the other hand, will get support from veterans Mylene Paat and Ara Galang.
 Meanwhile, unbeaten Nxled guns for an 8-0 sweep when in battles ZUS Coffee at 6 p.m.
 Advertisement 
 CRUCIAL GAME Creamline takes on Farm Fresh on Nov. 21, 2026, as the Cool Smashers aim for the twice-to-beat advantage in the semifinal round of 2026-27 Premier Volleyball League (PVL) All-Filipino Conference-Siklab Series. PHOTO BY RIO DELUVIO
